lines.t: Yeah…
Church bell on a Sunday, paint peelin’ off the steeple,
Whole town dressed clean, but they don’t know their Redeemer.
Granddaddy’s pew, mama’s hymn, daddy’s old religion,
But the Word still cut deep when it came with division.
YahuShua, open eyes…
Before the road runs out.
I been rollin’ through the backroads, dust on the tires,
Every little town got a cross reachin’ higher,
Brick church, white church, cathedral on the hill,
Old stone walls but the hearts stand still.
Built in eighteen-somethin’, bell been ringin’ that long,
People show up every week, sing the same old song,
Say “Amen,” shake hands, then they leave unchanged,
Carry tradition like a chain, call the chain “His name.”
Stained glass picture, gold on the frame,
But a picture of the Savior ain’t the Savior’s flame.
They taught a system, taught a title, taught men how to bow,
But YahuShua said, “Come follow,” and He’s sayin’ it now.
Not your daddy’s denomination, not a preacher’s degree,
Not a choir full of voices if the heart won’t see.
Ain’t no building gonna stand when the truth gets loud,
Ain’t no crowd gonna save you just because it’s a crowd.
I see old women prayin’ with a hurt in their eyes,
I see young men numb, livin’ comfortable lies,
I see children learnin’ words before they learn obedience,
A whole nation fed crumbs, callin’ famine “convenience.”
And Babylon dressed pretty, perfume in the air,
Said, “Come sit in my pew, you ain’t gotta go there.”
But the narrow road waits where the proud won’t tread,
And the living Word still speaks to the spiritually dead.
He put truth in reach, but He won’t drag your feet,
He’ll knock at the door, but you choose the seat.
Will you hold that lie ‘cause it came from your kin?
Or let the Light come in where the dark been?
Open my eyes, YahuShua, open my eyes,
Cut through the smoke, cut through the disguise.
The harlot sang sweet, had the whole town fooled,
But Your Word hit hard like a blacksmith tool.
Open my eyes, I don’t wanna pretend,
I don’t want religion that dies in the end.
You gave me the door, You gave me the Way,
Now I gotta choose if I’ll walk it today.
There’s a graveyard behind every old-town church,
Names in the stone, generations searched,
Some never heard truth with the veil pulled tight,
Some heard it clear and still loved the night.
That’s the part that shakes me, that’s the part that burns,
Truth ain’t a trophy for the man that learns;
Truth is a sword and a fire in the chest,
It separates the real from the dressed-up rest.
Internet wide open, Scripture in your hand,
No king can lock it, no priest can command.
Every tongue got access, every house got light,
Still people scroll past truth every single night.
Got sermons by the thousand, Bibles by the bed,
But no oil in the lamp, no life in the bread.
They want a blessing without bein’ made new,
Want Heaven in the end but no cross to go through.
Brother, don’t blame the devil for the choice you repeat,
Don’t blame your hometown when you love that seat.
Don’t blame mama’s wounds, don’t blame daddy’s rage,
YahuShua can break chains at whatever age.
Yeah, the trap was ancient, yeah, deception ran deep,
Yeah, wolves wore collars while the flock fell asleep.
But the Shepherd still calls through the noise and the shame,
And every soul must answer when He calls their name.
The mirror don’t lie when the Word comes near,
It shows what you worship, what you really fear.
He offers the water, but He won’t force the drink,
You got breath in your lungs—so stop and think.
Open my eyes, YahuShua, open my eyes,
Cut through the smoke, cut through the disguise.
The harlot sang sweet, had the whole town fooled,
But Your Word hit hard like a blacksmith tool.
Open my eyes, I don’t wanna pretend,
I don’t want religion that dies in the end.
You gave me the door, You gave me the Way,
Now I gotta choose if I’ll walk it today.
I lament for the elders who died in a fog,
For the faithful-looking men who never knew God.
For the daughters taught fear, for the sons taught pride,
For the wounded who came and were pushed aside.
For every false peace built on man-made words,
For every truth buried under polished church dirt.
But I praise You, YahuShua—You didn’t leave us blind,
You still call the lost, You still rescue the mind.
Your Word ain’t locked in a tower somewhere,
It’s bread for the hungry, it’s breath in the air.
The Kingdom is hidden from the proud man’s face,
But the seeker finds mercy, truth, and grace.
Not because he earned it, not because he knew,
But because he bowed low and let Your Word make him new.
So tear down the idol, let the old self die,
Walk out of the darkness with Your name held high.
Open my eyes, YahuShua, open my eyes,
I won’t trade Your truth for a comfortable lie.
Let the bells keep ringin’, let the old walls fall,
Your voice is the only voice I follow through it all.
